decision.title: How the 2027 minimum wage was set
items: The Minimum Wage Commission (27 worker, employer and public members) voted for 10,700 KRW/hour at its 14th plenary session on July 14, 2026. The final vote was workers' 10,730 KRW vs employers' 10,700 KRW; the employers' proposal won 15 votes.

The Ministry of Employment and Labor published the proposal on July 16, took objections until July 27, and finalized it on August 5. The Minimum Wage Act requires a decision by August 5 each year (Art. 8).
An announced minimum wage takes effect on January 1 of the following year (Art. 10). From January 1 to December 31, 2027 it is 10,700 KRW/hour, up 380 KRW (3.7%) from 10,320 KRW in 2026.
The same amount applies to every workplace regardless of industry, and no separate minimum was set for piece-rate workers.

scope.title: Who it applies to
items: Every business that employs workers, including those with fewer than 5 employees, part-timers and short-hour workers (Minimum Wage Act Art. 3(1)).
Exceptions: businesses employing only cohabiting relatives, domestic workers, and seafarers covered by the Seafarers' Act (Art. 3).
Any contract term below the minimum wage is void and treated as an agreement to pay the minimum wage (Art. 6(3)).

inclusion.title: Which wages count
items: Only wages paid regularly at least once a month are compared (Art. 6(4)). Quarterly or annual bonuses do not count.
Monthly regular bonuses and cash welfare allowances such as meals, lodging and transport have been phased in since 2019 and count in full from 2024.
Overtime, night and holiday premiums and other pay outside contractual hours, as well as in-kind meals or housing, do not count.
For monthly salaries, divide the qualifying monthly pay by the monthly hours (209h for 40h/week) and compare it with the hourly minimum.

probation.title: Probation reduction
items: Only workers on a contract of 1 year or more and within 3 months of starting probation may be paid down to 90% of the minimum (Act Art. 5(2), Enforcement Decree Art. 3) — 9,630 KRW/hour in 2027.
No reduction is allowed for contracts shorter than 1 year or after the 3-month window.

Occupations designated by the Minister as simple labor cannot be reduced even during probation. The designation follows the simple-labor group of the Korean Standard Classification of Occupations (reference).

violation.title: Penalties and reporting
items: Paying below the minimum wage, or cutting existing pay because of it, is punishable by up to 3 years in prison or a fine of up to 20 million KRW, or both (Art. 28(1)).
Unpaid amounts are wage claims and must be claimed within 3 years (Labor Standards Act Art. 49).
Call the MOEL helpline (1350) and file a petition with the regional labor office covering your workplace, or apply online through the MOEL labor portal.
Keep your contract, schedules, pay slips and bank transfer records — they help the investigation.

items.a: 10,700 KRW per hour, up 380 KRW (3.7%) from 10,320 KRW in 2026. For 40 hours a week that is 2,236,300 KRW a month (209 hours) or 26,835,600 KRW a year. It was announced on August 5, 2026 and applies from January 1, 2027.

items.q: Does the 2,236,300 KRW monthly figure include weekly holiday pay?
items.a: Yes. 209 hours is 40 working hours plus 8 holiday hours (48) times the average weeks per month (365 ÷ 7 ÷ 12 ≈ 4.345). So 10,700 × 209 = 2,236,300 KRW is pre-tax pay including holiday pay. In 2026 it is 2,156,880 KRW.

items.q: What is the minimum monthly pay for a 20-hour part-time job?
items.a: At 15 hours or more a week you get weekly holiday pay, so 20 hours adds 4 holiday hours for about 104 hours a month: 10,700 × 104 = 1,112,800 KRW in 2027. Below 15 hours a week, only hours worked are paid.

items.q: Can employers pay less than the minimum during probation?
items.a: Only for workers on a contract of 1 year or more and within 3 months of starting probation, down to 90% (9,630 KRW/hour in 2027). No reduction is allowed for contracts under 1 year or for simple-labor occupations designated by the Minister (Act Art. 5(2), Decree Art. 3).

items.q: Do businesses with fewer than 5 employees have to pay the minimum wage?
items.a: Yes. The Minimum Wage Act covers every business that employs workers, even a shop with one employee. Unlike overtime premiums, there is no size exemption. Only businesses employing cohabiting relatives, domestic workers and similar cases are excluded.

items.q: Does the minimum wage differ by industry?
items.a: No. Article 4 of the Act allows differentiation by type of business, but the 2027 minimum wage of 10,700 KRW/hour applies equally to all workplaces regardless of industry.

items.q: Do meal allowances and bonuses count toward the minimum wage?
items.a: Regular bonuses paid at least monthly and cash welfare allowances such as meals and transport count in full from 2024. Quarterly or annual bonuses, overtime, night and holiday pay, and in-kind meals do not count.

items.q: How do I report unpaid minimum wage?
items.a: Call the MOEL helpline (1350) and file a petition with the regional labor office covering your workplace, also possible online. Violations carry up to 3 years in prison or a 20 million KRW fine (Act Art. 28), and unpaid amounts must be claimed within 3 years.
